description: Original IOAI-style practice prompts for learning. These are not official past-contest tasks.

problems.title: Clean the Messy Table
problems.prompt: A CSV contains missing values, duplicate rows, and inconsistent category labels. Build a reproducible cleaning pipeline and report how many rows were changed or removed.
tasks: Inspect shape, column types, and missingness.
Remove exact duplicates and justify any row removals.
Standardize category labels.
Return a clean DataFrame and a short data-quality summary.
constraints: Do not silently drop rows with missing values.
Keep the original data unchanged.
problems.starter_code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
# TODO: inspect and clean the data
hints: Count missing values before modifying the data.
Use explicit mappings for inconsistent category labels.

problems.title: Build a Majority-Class Baseline
problems.prompt: Given a labelled classification dataset, build a baseline that always predicts the most frequent training class. Evaluate it on held-out data and explain why this score may be misleading.
tasks: Split data into train and test sets.
Find the majority class using training labels only.
Predict that class for every test example.
Report accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 where defined.
constraints: Do not inspect test labels to choose the prediction.
Use a fixed random seed.
problems.starter_code:
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report

# X and y: load or construct a labelled dataset
# TODO: split, build baseline predictions, evaluate
hints: A high accuracy can be unhelpful when one class dominates.
State how undefined precision or recall is handled.

problems.title: Predict a Continuous Target
problems.prompt: Train a regression model on tabular data and compare it with a simple baseline. Your goal is a trustworthy evaluation, not just a low training error.
tasks: Identify numeric and categorical features.
Create a train/test split.
Fit a baseline and a linear regression model.
Compare MAE and inspect residuals.
constraints: Fit preprocessing only on training data.
Do not select the model using test-set results.
problems.starter_code:
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error
from sklearn.dummy import DummyRegressor
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

# TODO: prepare X and y, split, fit, compare
hints: Keep the same split for both models.
Inspect whether residuals show a systematic pattern.

problems.title: Find the Better Decision Threshold
problems.prompt: A binary classifier outputs probabilities. Select a decision threshold that balances false positives and false negatives for a clearly stated use case.
tasks: Generate probabilities on a validation set.
Evaluate thresholds from 0.1 to 0.9.
Plot precision, recall, and F1.
Explain the chosen threshold and its limitations.
constraints: Do not tune the threshold on the final test set.
Report the class balance.
problems.starter_code:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import precision_score, recall_score, f1_score

thresholds = np.arange(0.1, 1.0, 0.1)
# TODO: calculate metrics for each threshold
hints: A threshold of 0.5 is not automatically optimal.
Choose the metric based on the costs of each error.

problems.title: Spot Data Leakage
problems.prompt: Review an ML pipeline where scaling and feature selection are performed on the full dataset before splitting. Identify the leakage, explain why it inflates evaluation, and rewrite the pipeline safely.
tasks: Mark every operation that learns from data.
Explain which information crosses the split boundary.
Use a scikit-learn Pipeline and train/test split.
Describe how cross-validation should be performed.
constraints: Do not use test data for fitting preprocessing or feature selection.
problems.starter_code:
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.feature_selection import SelectKBest
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

# TODO: put learned preprocessing and estimator in one pipeline
hints: Any transformation that estimates parameters from data belongs inside the training workflow.
Use a pipeline during cross-validation.

problems.title: Improve a Noisy Image Classifier
problems.prompt: Train a small image classifier and investigate one controlled improvement. Compare a baseline with one change such as augmentation, normalization, or regularization.
tasks: Create a reproducible baseline.
Choose one improvement and explain the hypothesis.
Keep the evaluation split fixed.
Compare validation metrics and inspect error examples.
constraints: Change one major factor at a time.
Do not tune repeatedly against the final test set.
problems.starter_code:

from torch import nn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader

hints: Start with a small dataset such as a subset of CIFAR-10.
Use a validation set for iteration and reserve test data for final reporting.

problems.title: Cluster Without Labels
problems.prompt: Apply K-means to an unlabelled dataset. Compare cluster assignments before and after feature scaling, and discuss whether the clusters are meaningful.
tasks: Visualize feature ranges.
Fit K-means with a fixed seed.
Scale features using a pipeline and fit again.
Compare cluster sizes and inertia.
constraints: Do not claim that lower inertia alone proves better clusters.
problems.starter_code:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline

# TODO: compare KMeans with and without scaling
hints: K-means relies on distances.
Feature scales can dominate those distances.

problems.title: Detect Machine-Altered Text
problems.prompt: Build a text classifier to distinguish two labelled text conditions. Establish a simple baseline, avoid duplicate leakage, and report performance with an error analysis.
tasks: Inspect label distribution and duplicate texts.
Create a split that avoids near-identical examples crossing partitions.
Build a TF-IDF plus linear classifier baseline.
Report precision, recall, F1, and representative errors.
constraints: Use only the supplied labelled data.
Do not claim the model reliably detects AI-generated text in general from one dataset.
problems.starter_code:
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

# texts and labels should be loaded from a labelled dataset
model = make_pipeline(TfidfVectorizer(), LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))
# TODO: split carefully, fit, evaluate
hints: Near duplicates can make test results look unrealistically strong.
Dataset-specific patterns may not generalize to other sources.

problems.title: Find a Useful Feature Set
problems.prompt: Run a feature-ablation study to determine whether groups of features help or hurt validation performance. Keep all other choices fixed.
tasks: Define a baseline feature set.
Remove one feature or group at a time.
Repeat with cross-validation.
Summarize average score and variability.
constraints: Do not choose features using the test set.
Document all configurations.
problems.starter_code:
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_validate

feature_groups = {}  # map names to feature columns
# TODO: evaluate each configuration using the same folds
hints: A feature may help in combination with another feature.
Small score changes may be noise; report variability.

problems.title: Reconstruct an Audio Sequence
problems.prompt: Given short audio segments and metadata, infer the most likely order of segments. Design a scoring method, test it on labelled examples, and analyze ambiguous cases.
tasks: Inspect available metadata and audio features.
Build a simple similarity or classification baseline.
Evaluate ordering accuracy on held-out examples.
Inspect cases where the sequence is ambiguous.
constraints: Do not use external data unless explicitly allowed.
Keep validation examples separate from tuning.

hints: Start with a simple pairwise score before optimizing a complex sequence model.
Segment similarity alone may not uniquely determine order.

problems.prompt: Build a word or sentence similarity baseline and study where it fails. Compare a simple lexical method with an embedding-based method if an allowed embedding model is available.
tasks: Define a small labelled similarity set.
Implement a lexical baseline.
Compare with a permitted embedding representation.
Inspect examples with similar surface form but different meaning.
constraints: Document model and resource availability.
Do not equate embedding similarity with truth or synonymy.

hints: Lexical overlap can fail on paraphrases.
Polysemy and context affect semantic similarity.

problems.title: Design a Competition-Ready Evaluation
problems.prompt: Create an evaluation plan for a new AI task. Specify a baseline, split strategy, metric, reproducibility controls, and checks against leakage or overfitting.
tasks: Describe task type and target output.
Choose a baseline that can be implemented quickly.
Select a metric aligned with the task objective.
Write a reproducibility and leakage checklist.
constraints: State assumptions and limitations.
Do not report hypothetical results as measured results.

hints: A baseline helps determine whether a complex approach adds value.
